docker-compose.description: The testenv fixtures are named <service>.compose.yaml, and the manager's default patterns anchor on a name STARTING with compose, so they matched nothing and the surface read as absent rather than unwatched. $default keeps the defaults and adds that naming.

packageRules.description: hyperi-ci's own composites and reusable workflows reference each other at @main on purpose, and the interface gate makes that safe (docs/workflow-composites.md). Never pin or bump them. The org preset disables the same depName for the consumer caller, and this rule keeps the internal refs unpinned whatever happens to that one.

The app-token action mints the bot token the release tail tags and publishes with. Its step runs only when a release publishes, so no PR exercises a new major and green CI proves nothing about it. A major waits for a human to tick it on the Dependency Dashboard, having read the release notes.

A test fixture's image tracks what production DEPLOYS, not whatever is newest — a fixture running a version no cluster runs tests nothing anyone ships. So these are WATCHED, not auto-bumped: Renovate lists them on the Dependency Dashboard and raises a PR only when a human ticks the box, because which line to track is a DFE deployment fact this repo cannot see.
